title: The southern Milky Way above ALMA
caption: The southern Milky Way above ALMA antennas, Chajnantor plateau
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Ranked #27 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: ALMA antennas stand beneath a rich sky on the 5000-meter-high Chajnantor plateau in Chile's Atacama region. According to the source, the view takes in the constellations Carina and Vela, with the Milky Way's dark, wispy dust clouds running from upper left to lower right through the middle of the frame.

The caption points out several stars. The bright orange star at upper left is Suhail in Vela, and the similar orange star at upper middle is Avior in Carina. Nearby, three bright blue stars form an L, the left two in Vela and the right one in Carina. Directly below them, at the center of the image, glows the pink Carina Nebula.

ESO, the European partner in ALMA, provided 25 of the 66 antennas planned for the finished array. The two nearest the camera, marked DA-43 and DA-41, are European antennas. At the time, the telescope was already observing with part of its array, ahead of completion in 2013.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape photograph by Babak Tafreshi. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: A camera exposure brings out colors such as the pink of the Carina Nebula, which the eye sees only faintly, if at all.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: ESO Photo Ambassador Babak Tafreshi took the picture. He founded The World At Night, a program that photographs historic sites against the night sky. ALMA brings together Europe, North America and East Asia in partnership with Chile, led by ESO, NRAO and NAOJ, with the Joint ALMA Observatory managing construction and operations.
alt: Radio antennas under a starry sky with the Milky Way's dark dust lanes running diagonally, orange and blue stars, and a pink glowing nebula at the center.
